model_annotation: This plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several language model variants, comparing their convergence behavior. The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000 on a linear scale, with tick marks every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis represents the loss, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4 on a linear scale, with tick marks every 0.1 unit. Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different model configuration: purple for "Vanilla", blue for "StrmLLM (n=64)", orange for "SepLLM (n=64)", green for "SepLLM (n=64, H)", red for "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)", and dark blue for "SepLLM (n=128)". All lines start near a loss of 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep decline in the initial phase, followed by a gradual flattening as training progresses. The "Vanilla" model (purple) shows the lowest loss throughout, stabilizing around 2.5 by 140,000 iterations. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" (blue) consistently has the highest loss, ending near 2.6. The other SepLLM variants (orange, green, red, dark blue) lie between these two extremes, with the "SepLLM (n=128)" (dark blue) showing a slightly lower loss than the n=64 variants, approaching approximately 2.52 at the end. All lines are solid and exhibit minor fluctuations, indicating noise in the training process.
